newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Congo's U.N. envoy speaks of jubilation in Africa.
newsitem.headline: Congo's U.N. envoy speaks of jubilation in Africa.

text.p: Congo's U.N. ambassador, representing African states at the United Nations, called the appointment of Ghanaian Kofi Annan "a great day for all sons of Africa."

In an address to the General Assembly, Ambassador Daniel Abibi, said: "Since Friday in fact the great news has been crossing our deserts, our savannahs and our forests proclaiming that Africa, after an outstanding mandate of five years, has been confirmed by the choice of another of its sons."
Annan, 58, succeeds Egyotian Boutros Boutros-Ghali, 74, who was the first secretary-general from the African continent.
The United States blocked Boutros-Ghali's hopes for a second term by vetoing his candidacy last month, alleging he had not done enough to carry out reforms.
The U.N. Security Council on Friday voted for Annan and the 185-member General Assembly endorsed the choice on Tuesday.
Speaking in French, Abibi said Africans were following the events closely from Algeria in the north to South Africa, from the Cape Verde islands in the west to Kenya in the south.
"As was the case five years ago, December 17 is a great day for Africa and for all those who hail from Africa," he said.
"It is with confidence and serenity that we witness our brother, Kofi Annan, take over the reins of the United Nations on January 1, 1997," he said.
